newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Govt to oust Bank Queensland directors -paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Govt to oust Bank Queensland directors -paper.

text.p: The Queensland state government will use its 44 percent stake in the Bank of Queensland Ltd to remove three directors at the bank's annual meeting in December, the Courier-Mail newspaper said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said the government will put resolutions to the meeting that former Suncorp chairman Graham Tucker together with fellow directors Ted Ranson and Bernard Rowley be dismissed from the bank's board.
In their place, the government has proposed the election of government nominees Daryl McDonough, Neil Summerson and Don Harvey, the report said.

Tucker, Ranson and another Suncorp director, John Wruck, resigned from Suncorp last month after declaring publicly they were unable to form on opinion on whether a merger of their company with Metway Bank Ltd and Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) was in Suncorp's interest.

The newspaper report said the proposal to replace the three directors had been discussed with the Reserve Bank of Australia which has been monitoring both the merger plan and the government's dealing with the Bank of Queensland stake.
Bank of Queensland chairman Neil Roberts recently told Reuters an offer to buy back 30 percent of the bank's capital from the government at current market prices was still current.
